messages.author: 944a94c45996805c
messages.subject: roxygen for namespace
parts:
Hello,

I'm just getting started on turning some Stan models into an R package.   I've used the rstan_skeleton_package function and followed the directions in the readme file.  The basic setup seems to be working.  I'm largely learning by reading through the rstanarm github and I've noticed that the NAMESPACE file was generated with roxygen.  Do you recommend this as standard practice?  If so where should the code to create the required lines, especially useDynLib(packageName, .registration = TRUE),  be generated? 

Any advice about how to transition to roxygen or whether or not it's worth transitioning, would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

Jonathon O'Brien

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: roxygen for namespace
parts:
On Wednesday, March 15, 2017 at 4:56:10 PM UTC-4, jonatho...@gmail.com wrote:
Any advice about how to transition to roxygen or whether or not it's worth transitioning, would be greatly appreciated.

We would definitely recommend roxygen and there is actually a step where the cleanup script would break if you were not using roxygen. The useDynLib() line typically comes from the foo-package.R file (where foo is the name of your package) whose only R code is the terminating line

NULL

such as

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm/blob/master/R/rstanarm-package.R

All the documentation is online at Hadley's website

http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: roxygen for namespace
parts:
On Wednesday, March 15, 2017 at 8:42:46 PM UTC-4, Jonathon O'Brien wrote:
Thank you!  That file explains a lot.  

I just realized that there's another extremely basic piece that I don't understand.  How do I access the Stan model through R code?  There are Stan files and R files.  Is the Stan code is compiled on loading?    I saw a previous question where someone suggested calling sampling() on a pre-compiled object, but where do the objects live and how should they be accessed?

There should be a named list called stanmodels containing compiled stanmodel objects that is in your package's namespace but not exported. The names of the list elements are the same as the files in the exec/ directory but without the .stan extension. You can pass any of those to sampling(), optimizing(), or vb().

Ben

Try moving your NAMESPACE file to a safe place. Then, in R, call roxygen2::roxygenize(clean = TRUE) when the working directory is the root of your package. Then do R CMD build, R CMD check, etc.

Ben

It seems that I don't understand the basics of how to work with the model objects created when the package loads.

I'm working with a very simple Stan model, just to test everything out. The file is called "testModel.stan" In my usual workflow I would have code like this;

y_ <- rnorm(100,5,5)
N <- length(y_)
sFit <- stan(file = "testModel.stan")
summary(sFit)

This code works fine, in the respect that the posterior mean is close to 5.  However, when working in a package the code is altered and the results are off.

y_ <- rnorm(100,5,5)
N <- length(y_)
sFit <- sampling(stanmodels$testModel)
summary(sFit)

Jonathon

The testModel.stan file that you have in the master branch of your GitHub repository is different:

goodrich@T540p:/tmp$ cat compMS/exec/testModel.stan
